info.title: bia
info.description: Workflows as data, run from Postgres. Every endpoint fails with the same error body: a stable `code`, a `message`, and `diagnostics` when a Definition was at fault.

get.summary: The authorization server's endpoints and what it supports. Public.
The API's metadata, for tokens issued for the whole API. Public.
The MCP endpoint's metadata: which authorization server issues tokens for `/mcp`. Public.
Answers while the process serves HTTP, whatever the state of the database.

post.summary:
Starts a Run of the Workflow's Active Version from one of its webhook Triggers, with the
JSON body (`{}` when empty) as `input`, checked against the `input_schema`. A Trigger without
`hmac` needs its bound `webhook` Token or an `admin` Token as `Authorization: Bearer`; one
with `hmac` needs the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, as hex optionally prefixed `sha256=`, in
its `hmac.header`. Without a Token, a path that names no webhook Trigger of an Active Version
answers `missing_token`, like a Trigger that needs one.

401.description:
No Token, or one that is unknown, revoked or expired; `code` is `missing_token` or
`invalid_token`.

403.description:
The Token's Scope does not allow this route (`insufficient_scope`), or a request made
with the Session cookie carries no acceptable `Origin` (`origin_mismatch`).

404.description: `webhook_not_found`, to a caller with a Token.

get.summary:
Starts an authorization: redirects to the UI's consent screen at
`{ui_url}/oauth/consent?request=<id>`, where a signed-in person approves or denies. Needs no
credential. A problem with the client or its redirect URI is a 400 error body; any other
problem redirects to the client's `redirect_uri` with `error`, `error_description`, `state`
and `iss`.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: A Client ID Metadata Document URL (`https`), or an id from `POST /oauth/register`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Exactly one of the client's registered redirect URIs; a loopback one may use any port.

parameters.name: code_challenge
parameters.description: The PKCE challenge: the base64url SHA-256 of the code verifier.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `agent` (default) or `admin`; the person may approve less than is asked.

302.description: To the consent screen, or to the client's `redirect_uri` with an OAuth `error`.

503.description: `public_url_missing`, or, as plain text, a build without a UI and `ui_url`.

post.summary:
Registers a client. Open to anyone, since a client has to register before it can ask; the
person who approves it is told it registered itself and is unverified. At most 20 per
address per hour.

Revokes the Grant the token belongs to, and with it every access token and refresh token it
issued: a client that is done wants all of it gone. Answers 200 whether or not the token
was known. Needs no credential, since holding the token is the proof.

Issues an access token and a refresh token. Needs no credential: the code, its PKCE
verifier and the client id are the proof.

post.summary:
Asks for a Version to be published and/or activated. A Draft target must pass the checks
publishing makes, or the request fails with `invalid_definition` and the Diagnostics and
nothing is created. `activate` needs a Published Version. The Workflow's earlier pending
request becomes `withdrawn`. Replacing the Draft later makes the request `stale`. Needs an
`agent` or `admin` Token; an admin decides it with `approve` or `reject`.

409.description: `version_published` for a Published Version asked to be published, or `version_not_published` for a Draft asked to be activated.

422.description: `invalid_definition`: the Draft cannot be published; `diagnostics` says why.

post.summary:
Asks for the Run to stop. The response is 202: a Worker cancels the Attempt in flight and
the Run becomes `cancelled` a moment later (a sleeping Run at once), which `get_run` shows.
A Run that already finished is refused with `run_finished`.

post.summary:
Resumes a `failed` Run from the Step that failed, on its own Version even if another is
active now. Steps that succeeded do not run again; the failed Step gets a fresh retry
budget and its Attempt numbers carry on. A Run that is not `failed`, or failed before any
Step ran (e.g. invalid input), is refused with `run_not_resumable`.

the original's plus `retry_of`, the original's id. Re-running on a newer Version means
triggering the Workflow instead. A Run that has not finished is refused with
`run_not_finished`.

post.summary:
Signs in with the password and sets the `bia_session` cookie: `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`,
`Secure` when `public_url` is HTTPS, and no `Domain`. The Session lasts 14 days without use
and 90 days at most. After five failed attempts each further one waits longer, up to a
minute, per User and client address. Public, since it is how a browser gets a Token.

401.description: `invalid_credentials`: the password is wrong, or no User has one yet.

delete.summary: Revokes the Session the request is made with and clears its cookie. Needs a Session.

post.summary:
Sets the password of the install's User, creating it on a fresh install, with the code
from the Setup Link that `bia serve` logs, and signs that User in: the response sets the
`bia_session` cookie, as `POST /v1/session` does. Public, since no one can sign in yet.
Refuses once a User has a password; `bia serve --reset-admin` clears it and logs a new link.

403.description: `invalid_setup_code`: the code is wrong; `setup_code_expired`: it is from before the server last started, so use the link it logged since.

422.description: `password_too_short`: the password has fewer than 12 characters.

`no_manual_trigger`.

Saves the request body, a Definition, as a new Draft of the Workflow, numbered after its
latest Version. The Workflow is created by its first Draft. Any number of Drafts may exist
at once. Semantic errors do not stop a Draft from being saved: they come back in
`diagnostics`. A body that does not parse as a Definition is refused with
`invalid_definition`, and one whose `id` is not the Workflow's with `workflow_id_mismatch`.

401.description:
No Token, or one that is unknown, revoked or expired; `code` is `missing_token` or
`invalid_token`.

403.description:
The Token's Scope does not allow this route (`insufficient_scope`), or a request made
with the Session cookie carries no acceptable `Origin` (`origin_mismatch`).

put.summary:
Replaces a Draft's Definition in place, keeping its number. Refused with
`version_published` once the Version is Published. The body is treated as in
`create_draft`.

post.summary:
Makes a Published Version the Workflow's Active Version: new Runs start on it and the
scheduler follows its cron Triggers. Activating an older Version is a rollback; Runs
already started keep their Version (ADR-0009). Needs an `admin` Token.

`invalid_token`.

403.description:
The Token's Scope does not allow this route (`insufficient_scope`), or a request made
with the Session cookie carries no acceptable `Origin` (`origin_mismatch`).

post.summary:
Dry-runs a stored Version, a Draft or a Published one: pure Actions run for real, side
effects return Mocks, and waits resolve instantly. Nothing is stored and nothing outside
the server is touched. The Definition must have no error Diagnostics (`invalid_definition`
otherwise); a Mock that names a missing or unMockable Step, or is not in the documented
format, is refused with `invalid_mock`.

requestBody.description: The input and Mocks; send `{}` for none.

post.summary:
Publishes a Draft after validating it for publishing: unknown Queues and Workflows and
disabled or dangerous Actions are errors, and any error refuses with `invalid_definition`
and the Diagnostics. A Published Version never changes again. Needs an `admin` Token, which
is also what keeps Versions that use dangerous Actions in human hands.

409.description: `version_published`, or `version_changed` when the Draft was replaced meanwhile.

ActionEffect.description:
Whether an Action can change anything outside the Run. A Dry Run executes `pure` Actions
and gives `side_effecting` ones a Mock.

ActionEntry.description: An Action a Step can name in `action`.

enabled.description: A Version that uses a disabled Action cannot be published.

examples.description: Example calls, also the source of Mocks in a Dry Run.

output_schema.description: The JSON Schema of the Step's Output, read by later Steps as `steps.<id>.output`.

param_schema.description: The JSON Schema a Step's `params` must satisfy once its Templates are resolved.

oneOf.description:
The Scope to grant: what was requested, or `agent` to downgrade `admin`. Asking for more
than was requested is refused. Defaults to what was requested.

ApprovalRequestInfo.description:
An Approval Request, with what a review page shows: the Workflow, the Version, the action,
who asked and why, how long ago, and how it was decided.

closed_at.description: When the status left `pending`, whatever the reason.

comment.description: The admin's comment on the decision.

content_hash.description:
SHA-256 of the Draft's Definition when the request was made, as hex. Absent for

created_at.description: The request's age is now minus this.

decided_by.description: The User who approved or rejected it.

number.description: The Version the request is about.

requested_by.description: The User the requesting Token acts for.

requester_name.description: The name of the Token the request was made with, e.g. `claude-desktop`.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description: `true`: every authorization response, errors included, carries `iss` (RFC 9207).

client_id_metadata_document_supported.description: `true`: a `client_id` that is an `https` URL names a Client ID Metadata Document.

device_authorization_endpoint.description:
The device authorization grant (RFC 8628), which only the built-in `bia-cli` client may
use.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description: `none`: clients are public and prove themselves with PKCE.

new.description: The new password: at least 12 characters.

host.description: For `cimd`: the host the client's metadata was fetched from.

name.description: The name the client gave itself.

verified.description: `false` for a client that registered itself: its name is unchecked.

ConsentRequest.description: What a person is asked to approve.

redirect_uri.description: Where the person is sent back to, with the result.

requested_scope.description: What the client asked for; the person may approve less.

resource.description: What the tokens will be good for: the API, or the MCP endpoint only.

CreatedToken.description: A Token just created, with its value.

value.description:
Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <value>`. Shown only in this response: bia keeps a
hash of it, so a lost value cannot be recovered, only replaced.

DeadLetterSelection.description: Dead letters of the Queue to act on.

ids.description: Message ids, 1 to 200. Ids that are not dead letters of this Queue are skipped.

purged.description: How many dead letters were deleted.

replayed.description:
The new ids of the replayed Messages in the Queues they were dead-lettered from, in the
order of their old ids. Fewer than selected when some were skipped.

Decision.description: Where to send the person: the client's redirect URI with the result.

comment.description: Why, for the requester. Up to 2000 characters.

DefinitionDryRunRequest.description: What a Dry Run of a Definition that need not be stored takes.

definition.description: A Definition (see `GET /v1/schema`). Its Workflow need not exist.

scope.description: `agent` (default) or `admin`; the person may approve less than is asked.

DeviceAuthorizationResponse.description: What the device shows the person, and polls with (RFC 8628 section 3.2).

device_code.description: Secret: the device polls the token endpoint with it. Never shown to the person.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the codes stop working: 600.

user_code.description: What the person types at `verification_uri`, e.g. `BCDF-GHJK`.

DeviceConsentRequest.description: A device authorization a person is asked about.

id.description: Pass it to `GET /oauth/device/{id}` and the approve and deny routes.

requested_scope.description: What the client asked for; the person may approve less.

resource.description: What the tokens will be good for: the API, or the MCP endpoint only.

DeviceDecision.description: How a device authorization was answered. The device learns the result by polling.

Diagnostic.description: One validation finding about a Definition.

diagnostics.description: Validation findings that are not errors, such as problems only publishing needs solved.

dry_run.description: Always `true`; marks the Timeline as not a real Run's.

The entries a real Run's Timeline would hold, in the same shape and order. Waits take
no real time, but their entries show the time they would have taken.

DryRunRequest.description: What a Dry Run of a stored Version takes.

The Run input. Defaults to `{}`. Checked against the Definition's `input_schema`, as a
real Run's is.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response.

diagnostics.description: The Diagnostics behind the error, in document order. Absent when none apply.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Its wording may change; match on `code`.

ErrorCode.description:
A stable identifier for what went wrong with a request. Agents match on it, so codes may be
added, but renaming or removing one needs an ADR (ADR-0042).

FailedRun.description: A failed Run and the entry that failed it.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` to get the next page. Absent on the last page.

client_host.description: For `cimd`: the host the client's metadata came from.

refresh_token.description:
Single-use: exchanging it returns a new one. Presenting an old one again revokes the
Grant. Unused for 90 days it stops working.

MessageCountsInfo.description:
How many Messages the Queue holds, by state, when it was read. The four counts do not
overlap and add up to the Queue's depth.

dead_lettered.description:
Dead letters, whether kept in this Queue or moved here as its Dead-Letter Queue. Only
counted here, even when a consumer of a Dead-Letter Queue receives them.

delayed.description: Waiting out a publish delay or a retry backoff.

in_flight.description: Held by a consumer within its visibility timeout.

in_flight.description: Whether a consumer holds it right now.

When a consumer can receive it next: after its delay or retry backoff, or once the
visibility timeout of the delivery holding it ends. Absent for a dead letter kept in a
Queue without a Dead-Letter Queue, which is not delivered again.

next_after.description: Pass as `after` for the next page; absent on the last page.

MockSchema.description:
What a Step returns in a Dry Run instead of calling its Action. Give exactly one of
`output`, `error` or `attempts`.

Without a Mock, a `pure` Action runs for real and a `side_effecting` one returns the
Output of its first example, or, having no example, fails with the `no_mock` code. A Mock
also applies to a `pure` Action, which lets a Dry Run force it to fail. Only Steps that
call an Action can be Mocked: not `flow.*` Steps or Blocks.

attempts.description:
One `{ "output" }` or `{ "error" }` per Attempt: the first Attempt gets the first, and
the last repeats for the Attempts after it. Use it to fail twice and then succeed.

error.description:
The error every Attempt fails with: `{ "class": "retryable" | "fatal", "message",
"details"? }`. A `retryable` error follows the Step's retry policy exactly as a real one
does.

output.description: The Output every Attempt returns. Any JSON value, `null` included.

note.description: Why the change should go ahead, for the admin. Up to 2000 characters.

number.description: The Version's number: a Draft to publish, or a Published Version to activate.

name.description: What the Token is for, e.g. `claude-desktop`. Need not be unique.

oneOf.description: Required with the `webhook` Scope, and refused with any other.

error.description:
An OAuth error code such as `invalid_grant`, `invalid_request`, `invalid_scope`,

error_description.description: Human-readable explanation. Its wording may change; match on `error`.

How long a delivered Message stays hidden from other consumers, a Duration such as

session.name: bia_session
session.description: The Session cookie `POST /v1/session` sets: an `admin` Token for browsers. Wherever `token` is accepted, this is too, except on `/mcp`. A request with an unsafe method must carry an `Origin` equal to the origin of `public_url` or `ui_url`, or it fails with `origin_mismatch`.
